articles.title: Futurity Trophy: Jamie Lynch's runner-by-runner guide
articles.summary: With the final domestic Group 1 contest of the season looming, Sky Sports Racing's Senior Form Analyst Jamie Lynch analyses the chances of each of the seven runners; Watch the race at 3.35pm on Saturday - LIVE on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
If it's an important race for Aidan O'Brien - and 12 wins says it is - then it's an important race for each season and each generation, a Group 1 with a rich history of generating Classic winners.

Sure enough, Ballydoyle holds the keys to the William Hill Futurity Trophy once again, three keys to be precise, in a field of just seven, but the rest are more than merely making up the numbers.

Here's an in-depth rundown of the Group 1 participants, for the feature race of Saturday, live at 1.30pm on Sky Sports Racing .

Jockey: William Buick | Trainer: Charlie Appleby

Misfits matter because they can be innovative and inspirational, holding within them the ability to challenge, or challenging ability in the case of Al Hudaiba, whose shimmying and swerving are all part of his routine, taken to extremes the day he unshipped Tom Marquand.

And then there's the feeling of his tools and this test being a misfit, of competing forces, at least compared to the whizzing around Keeneland on fast ground for the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf, for which he earned a free berth after his Woodbine win including ingrained slalom. I can't see it, but more meaningful is that Charlie Appleby clearly can, and he won the Futurity in 2023 with Ancient Wisdom.

Lewis Edmunds | William Muir & Chris Grassick

William Muir has promised us that this is a top horse, which isn't unusual for him, as we know, but the groundwork has been good, and now his sire gets to do the talking, as the ground and the galloping nature of this test means it's time for the Cracksman in him to come out.

Ombudsman running riot last week was a reminder of just how scintillating Cracksman was in a soft-ground Champion Stakes, not once but twice, and Breacher hinted at being cut from a similar cloth with his staying-on third in the Solario, the style to add to the substance of another third in the Champagne, behind Desert Castle and the reopposing Sergei Diaghilev. Moving up to a mile may turn the boy into a man.

Burning Up felt the pinch and the pressure of the second-fastest Royal Lodge since the race was relocated to Newmarket (in 2011), on ground that was more like firm than the official good to firm, but his work out of the Dip that took him from fifth to second - beaten only by Heffner - suggested the Futurity framework would amp up his power, by plugging more into his stamina, from a classy middle-distance family.

Additionally, he looked really good and moved really well when conditions were on the soft side for his latter win at Haydock. With his profile and propulsion, he's got a chance of stemming the Ballydoyle tide.

The September slump was real for Aidan O'Brien, who sighted a low-level infection: his strike-rate in Ireland dropped to 14%, when more like 20% is the norm, and the run-to-form ratio likewise dipped below 60%, from a resting rate around 75%. That in itself is some mitigation for a dull display by Giant Sequoia in the National Stakes, when the choice of Moore over Royal Lodge winner Haffner, though the Moore merry-go-round now aligns with Noble Exhibit.

Giant Sequoia had a tall reputation from day one - even from Ballydoyle not many go off at 4-9 on their debut - but the Futurity was more functional than flashy, his star perhaps dimming, though he's bred to be suited by this step up in trip, being out of an Irish Oaks runner-up.

In the race to be champion trainer, O'Brien has got three high cards, whereas Andrew Balding is playing a joker, but it's hard to believe that Gran Dia can muscle in on the meaty prize money considering this is a world away from Salisbury, where he made a winning start.

That in itself is a big positive from the yard, which has had only six other winning two-year-old newcomers this year (including Moonrise and Forbidden Fire), but neither the time nor the form of Gran Dia's debut justifies him jumping up and missing quite the number of rungs of the ladder that he is.

It's the classic approach for the classic trainer when it comes to the Futurity. Of Aidan O'Brien's dozen winners, half of them came via the Beresford, including the very first, Saratoga Springs, way back in 1997. Noble Exhibit is virtually a replica of the latest, Hawk Mountain, including for style, as a front-runner, and though his Beresford success wasn't by so wide a margin, Noble Exhibit was gearing down by the end and actually brings a 1lb higher rating with him to Doncaster, if only equal to Al Hudaiba on official figures.

He's self-evident, a decision by dropdown not dynamism, a process of elimination rather than exhilaration, but the who, how and why of figuring out the Futurity all point to him: who trains him, how he got here and why Moore has picked him.

Exposed and established by now, but that was also the presumption around his uncle Johannes Vermeer before he was second in this in 2015 (and won the Criterium International eight days later). The last twice, Sergei Diaghilev has been beaten only by two of Godolphin's highest hopes, Desert Castle in the Champagne and Rock Montreal in the Autumn, with the advantage of dictating in both races, when the sole Ballydoyle representative. He's the support act this time.

The start point - and usually the end point - of the Futurity is the Ballydoyle contingent, numbering three this time, but none of them are particularly starry nor scary, relative to most years.

It's not stretching it to say that Haffner would have been the stable's selected had he come this way, which is pertinent because BURNING UP chased him home in the Royal Lodge in circumstances far less favourable than this playing ground promises to be, making him an attractive alternative for Karl Burke, numerically the top British trainer for the juveniles again this year.

articles.title: Verstappen se planta con los baches en Austin: "El año pasado tuve impactos verticales de 9G"
articles.standfirst: Mostró su preocupación por lo que puede afectar el asfalto del COTA a lo coches y a la salud de los pilotos
articles.summary: Mostró su preocupación por lo que puede afectar el asfalto del COTA a lo coches y a la salud de los pilotos
articles.body: El COTA de Austin es uno de los circuitos más interesantes, bonitos y variados del calendario de F1 y de MotoGP. Se inauguró en 2012, con la F1 en plena batalla de Alonso con Vettel por el Mundial y siempre ha ofrecido carreras muy intensas y espectaculares. Lo que ocurre es que está construido sobre un terreno arcilloso y húmedo y con el paso de los años y las competiciones, las capas de su firme, las inferiores y las superiores, va haciendo un 'efecto alfombra' con las frenadas de todo lo que rueda por encima. Se ha intentado reasfaltar y reforzar, pero el problema persiste. Max Verstappen ha alzado la voz en la previa del GP de Estados Unidos de este fin de semana, pidiendo una solución definitiva y dejando unos datos preocupantes para la salud de los pilotos, sobre lo que tuvo que soportar su columna vertebral en 2025 en este trazado. "Está muy mal. Por supuesto, puedes poner la excusa de que el problema es el suelo, pero entonces deberías haberlo sabido y asegurarte de reforzarlo más. Me encanta este circuito, me encanta este lugar. Tiene uno de los mejores diseños de la historia y diría que es uno de los mejores escenarios y una de las mejores ciudades a las que vamos, pero para mí los baches que tenemos son inaceptables", clamaba el holandés "Con el paso del tiempo han ido rebajando un poco el asfalto aquí y allá, pero eso es poner una tirita a un problema mucho mayor, que es lo que hay debajo. Eso es lo que realmente hay que solucionar en primer lugar. Pero eso, por supuesto, significa que tienes que levantar completamente la pista. Cuesta mucho dinero y tiempo, pero, sinceramente, es la única manera de acabar con el problema, porque estos baches no son normales y están fuera de control", pedía Max a la organización, un remozado total de las capas inferiores de tierra, drenaje, hormigón y los tres asfaltos que componen una pista de alta competición. Para Max, los coches de 2026 podrían acrecentar el problema, pese a tener un mayor recorrido en las suspensiones que los de efecto suelo de 2025. "Probablemente sea peor, porque llevamos alturas muy bajas cuando pasamos por las curvas. En las rectas tenemos el modo SM, así que el coche se eleva, pero en la mayoría de las zonas de frenada, especialmente, tocamos más con el fondo contra el suelo que antes. Y la mayoría de los baches están en las frenadas o en las curvas, no en las propias rectas", analizaba. "Al frenar es un momento de muchísimo esfuerzo, especialmente cuando hay este tipo de baches tan extraños. No son simplemente baches provocados por el envejecimiento de la pista, sino por lo que hay debajo de la superficie, por el terreno que se mueve hacia arriba y hacia abajo. A veces es muy difícil saber qué te vas a encontrar. Y si te sales un poquito de la trazada, tampoco sabes qué hay ahí, porque prácticamente nadie pasa por esa zona. Así que no es nada agradable", reflejaba de forma gráfica. Verstappen explicó que lo ha sentido en sus huesos, en concreto en la columna, "El año pasado, por ejemplo, soportabas unas 5 o 6 G en una curva, pero yo sufrí algunos impactos en los que la carga vertical sobre mi columna vertebral superó las 9 G. Puedo asegurar que no tiene ninguna gracia y, especialmente a medida que te haces mayor, empiezas a pensar cada vez más en estas cosas. No es lo que quieres", desvelaba. Para un piloto como él de unos 70 kg, esas compresiones verticales superan los 600 kg de fuerza. "Creo que a veces la gente no termina de entenderlo. Por las pruebas que me he hecho en la columna vertebral, puedo decir que la parte inferior no tiene muy buen aspecto", añadía un Max realmente preocupado "Sé que forma parte de las carreras y que puede formar parte del deporte, pero también son daños adicionales provocados por los coches que hemos tenido durante los últimos años. Y si seguimos considerando aceptable correr en estas condiciones, vamos a sufrir mucho más sus consecuencias", predecía, "La gente puede decir que hay deportes que provocan daños todavía mayores en determinadas partes del cuerpo. Por supuesto, pero precisamente por eso no los practico, así que no, no es nada agradable", cerraba sobre el tema uno de los favoritos para este fin de semana.

articles.title: Hollie Doyle: Aidan O'Brien to scoop Futurity prize with Noble Exhibit
articles.summary: As she prepares to make her comeback from injury, Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle chats to Simon Mapletoft ahead of the weekend's action - which is headlined by the Futurity Trophy from Doncaster, live on Sky Sports Racing
articles.body:
It looks like being a lucky 13th for master trainer Aidan O'Brien in the William Hill Futurity Trophy Stakes (1.30) at Doncaster on Saturday - live on Sky Sports Racing .

The Ballydoyle maestro heads the market with NOBLE EXHIBIT , who will be partnered by Ryan Moore in his pursuit of a first Group 1.

The son of Frankel looks the perfect type for this end-of-season assignment following his impressive win in the Group 2 Beresford Stakes at The Curragh - like the Futurity, a traditional pointer to next season's Classics.

He coped well with the yielding ground that day so the soft conditions on Town Moor shouldn't be an issue for the handsome chestnut.

Karl Burke has been bullish in his assessment of Noble Exhibit's most dangerous rival Burning Up , who confirmed his liking for soft ground when defying a penalty in a Haydock Park novice before going close in better company at Newmarket.

His second to O'Brien's more experienced Haffner in the Group 2 Royal Lodge can be upgraded as he just got caught out in the dip before running on strongly. This more conventional track should be ideal for him to cement his own classic credentials.

Godolphin have obvious claims with the jet-setting Al Hudaiba , who won a Grade 1 in Canada last month after taking the Superlative Stakes at Newmarket in the summer. He's quirky though and doesn't appeal to me as much as his market rivals.

BENGAL TIGER will be hard to beat in the Listed William Hill Remembering Sue Wright Prospect Stakes (2.05) at Doncaster. Better known as the Doncaster Stakes, this 6f sprint for two-year-olds is the ideal stepping stone for the son of No Nay Never who won his maiden as Naas by an incredible 12 lengths.

This race looks set to be dominated by the Irish with Paddy Twomey's Hi Corbett Court proving his liking for testing ground when beating all but a better-fancied stable companion in a valuable sales race at The Curragh.

Richard and Peter Fahey take them on with Crystal Queen who was second in an Ayr nursery after struggling in Group races in the summer but she needs to take a big step forward.

Adam Kirby has his team in fine form and I'm expecting ANCIENT STATE to supplement his course and distance win at the Leger Festival in the Richard James Hone Memorial Handicap (12.55) at Doncaster.

The four-year-old has run well in Class 2 company since last month's success and will definitely enjoy the ease in the ground with a relatively light weight to shoulder.

Mick Appleby's Al Shabab Storm went close in the Portland at this track before chasing home his highly progressive stable mate Coul Angel at York and gets on well with talented 5lb claimer Harry Vigors. He's a big player but has to give a lot of weight to Ancient State.

Chapple-Hyam gelding value for repeat success

DESPERATE DAN won the William Hill Epic Boosts Handicap (3.19) at Doncaster last year off the very same mark and has what it takes to follow up for his shrewd trainer Peter Chapple-Hyam.

Lightly raced this year, he's got his ground and should be sharpened up by the addition of blinkers with top northern jockey Paul Mulrennan doing the steering.

Ralph Beckett's Shipbourne benefitted from more positive tactics on the All-Weather at Southwell last month and could build on that back at the scene of his 7f win at the track in the summer.

Jack Channon does well in competitive handicaps and has a live contender in the William Hill Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap (3.55) at Doncaster with GALYX .

He bolted up at Beverley in soft ground off a 5lb lower rating and this track will suit him just as well. Off 85 he's still well within his range to win again off a relatively low weight.

I also like Michael Bell's proven soft ground performer A Major Payne who won nicely at Goodwood and still looks quite progressive.

My return to race riding edges ever closer following another positive week of training and riding out on the gallops in Lambourn and Newmarket.

I'm still firmly focused on making my comeback in early November, five and a half months after breaking my left leg in that horrible fall at Bath in May.

I've been stepping up my rehabilitation at Oaksey House in Lambourn but nothing beats being back in the saddle and I'm enjoying getting back on a horse at my boss Archie Watson's Saxon Gate Stables.

I don't have an exact date for my return but once I've had my BHA fitness test next week I should know more. It's been a long, difficult road but I'm so excited to be getting back to what I'm so passionate about.

articles.title: Ferrari y McLaren, con las mayores mejoras; Aston y Williams sin novedades
articles.standfirst: Los de Maranello llegan con suelo, pontones y difusor rediseñados
articles.summary: Los de Maranello llegan con suelo, pontones y difusor rediseñados
articles.body: La temporada toca a su fin en cuanto a las evoluciones aerodinámicas, sobre todo cuando los títulos de pilotos y constructores parecen decididos por completo. A pesar de ello, los programas de piezas establecidos se siguen implementando en algunos equipos, pues estos coches y los chasis serán casi los mismos para todos en 2027. Mercedes no declara ninguna pieza nueva en Austin, pues siguen intentando armar el rompecabezas de su gran paquete nuevo de Bakú, que aún no han logrado desentrañar por completo. Los que llegan con las aportaciones más interesantes son Ferrari y McLaren, a los que sus últimas evoluciones no les han funcionado como esperaban. En el caso del SF-26 de Hamilton y Leclerc, la apuesta de muy fuerte con un suelo rediseñado por completo desde los ataques de la zona delantera y toda la parte inferior, a lo que se suma una nueva entrada de pontones más alta y refinada, para dejar más espacio por la zona inferior y un difusor adecuado a todos estos cambios. Necesitan volver a dominar en los circuitos de chasis, cosa que no ha sucedido en Sepang y Singapur, cuando en principio partían como uno de los coches más fuertes. Lo introducido ahora puede servirles para un buen final de temporada y volver a luchar por una victoria. El segundo con más novedades de entre los grandes es McLaren. que no han dado en el clavo con las piezas que llegaron tras el verano e introducen modificaciones en las suspensiones delanteras, en el difusor y en la esquina trasera del coche, con el fin de recobrar eficiencia tras dos grandes premios discretos para ellos. Red Bull, por su parte, llega con dos retoques, uno de rendimiento local y otro de fiabilidad, pero poco importantes. Los que no introducen ninguna pieza nueva son Aston Martin y Williams, mientras Cadillac o Audi, si llegan con mejoras en Texas.

articles.title: Renault lanzará en 2027 su nuevo Clio Rally5
articles.summary: Derivado del Clio VI
articles.body: Renault renovará el año que viene su exitoso Clio Rally5, que dará paso a la siguiente hornada después de siete temporadas en liza. La marca tiene previsto presentar su nuevo coche antes de Navidad, y empezar a comercializarlo directamente (al menos, en Francia) para 2027. La nueva reglamentación de la categoría Rally5, que comenzará a aplicarse la próxima temporada, marcará las líneas maestras del nuevo Renault Clio, basado en la sexta generación del modelo de producción. Aunque aún se desconocen los detalles técnicos y su precio, promete seguir siendo un coche 'copero', económico y fácil de mantener, en la línea de su antecesor.

articles.summary: F1 is back in the U.S., but if you're watching from home, cable won't help this year.
articles.body:
The 18th race of the Formula 1 season will be the United States Grand Prix, held this weekend at Circuit of the Americas in Austin. Max Verstappen took the win at the 2025 race — can he do it again in 2026? Practice and qualifying races will be on Friday and Saturday, Oct. 23-24, with the Grand Prix taking place Sunday, Oct. 25, at 4 p.m. ET.

If you're tuning in from home, you should know that this year, F1 is streaming exclusively on Apple TV in the U.S. So if you want to catch this weekend's race live, you'll need access to Apple TV (or F1 TV Premium , now free with an Apple TV subscription). In addition to watching on Apple TV, you can tune into F1 practice sessions and qualifying races via the Yahoo Sports Racing Hub .

Here's everything you need to know about this weekend's F1 United States Grand Prix, including how to watch on Apple TV, and check out the full 2026 F1 Grand Prix schedule.

How to watch the F1 United States Grand Prix

Location: Circuit of the Americas, Austin, Texas

The 2026 U.S. Grand Prix will begin at 4 p.m. ET/1 p.m. PT on Sunday, Oct. 25.

F1 races used to air on ESPN and ESPN2 in the U.S., but Apple TV has signed an exclusive five-year deal to be the U.S. broadcaster of Formula 1 starting this season. That means the U.S. Grand Prix and every other race of the 2026 F1 season will stream live on Apple TV.

For those without traditional cable, that makes watching F1 much easier. If you aren't already an Apple TV subscriber and don't want to shell out for yet another streaming service, we have a guide on how to get Apple TV for free in 2026 .

articles.title: Racing tips: Burning Up backed to rise to Futurity challenge
articles.summary: The Weekend Winners panel of Kate Tracey, Declan Rix and Sam Boswell offer their views ahead of action from Cheltenham and Doncaster - which plays host to the Futurity Trophy; Watch the episode in full on the At The Races YouTube channel
articles.body:
At the end of the show, each of the trio nominated their best bet, next best and longshot, with Declan Rix taking aim at Doncaster for his top fancy.

"My NAP is coming in the Prospect Stakes at 2.05 at Doncaster on Saturday and it's Hi Corbett Court for the Paddy Twomey and Billy Lee team. I think he has stronger form than Bengal Tiger from that sales race that he ran well in. He's got a bit of class about him, and he has a significant knee action which will help him on Saturday.

"The longshot comes in the opener at Doncaster with the Kevin Phillipart de Foy-trained Sovereign Spell . If you go back and look at this horse's form at Newmarket this season, he looks well handicapped. He goes well fresh and he comes here off a break."

"My NAP is Bengal Tiger in the Listed Prospect Stakes and it's purely down to the lack of quality in behind. The cheekpieces have seemed to help him, and this is a good opportunity for him to win again.

"My next best is going to be Katate Dori for Sam Thomas. He's in the staying chase and his trainer always starts the season well and he is fitted with first-time blinkers today. He is well handicapped on last year's form and I think he will go well."

" Burning Up in the Futurity Trophy at Doncaster is the NAP for me. I think the conditions will suit and he will handle the flatter track. He has good pace on paper and I hope he can go well here.

"I'm going to a bumper race for my next best and it's a Joe Tizzard-trained runner in Thyingman . His horses are flying at the minute, with four winners at Ffos Las the other day. He won at Hereford on soft ground on his first career start and the test will hopefully suit him."

articles.title: Aston Martin y Honda, unidad en medio del caos
articles.standfirst: El gigante japonés cumple 500 Grandes Premios en la clase reina en un momento altamente complicado
articles.summary: El gigante japonés cumple 500 Grandes Premios en la clase reina en un momento altamente complicado
articles.body: La Fórmula 1 tiende a ser cíclica en determinados momentos de la historia. Los éxitos lo enseñan. Pero también los fracasos, que son, muchas veces, los que también sirven para establecer un relato. En esa situación está Honda, una de las compañías más grandes del mundo (más de 33.000 millones de facturación) pero con nuevos problemas en el Gran Circo. Los tuvo en su alianza moderna con McLaren, cambió el paso en tiempos de Red Bull y los vuelve a tener en su nueva historia junto a Aston Martin. Su 2026 ya es conocido por todos. Existieron problemas, existen y también existirán con su unidad de potencia. Pero en los Estados Unidos también viven un momento simbólico, pues celebran sus 500 Grandes Premios en la Fórmula 1. Aunque realmente no, pues, por ejemplo en Indianápolis 2005 sus coches -en ese momento los BAR Honda- no salieron ante el escándalo de los neumáticos. Pero la celebración existe y se lo han tomado como el momento de mostrar unidad en medio de la tempestad. De hecho, en la foto oficial del viernes en Austin estaban todos. Desde los pilotos del AMR26, Fernando Alonso y Lance Stroll, hasta los pilares del proyecto en los despachos, como Adrian Newey, su líder técnico, Lawrence Stroll, dueño del equipo, o Koji Watanabe, CEO del departamento de carreras de Honda. Quieren reivindicar que son uno, algo que repiten desde todas las esquinas de la escudería. Pero que todavía en pista no se ha completado al 100. De hecho, el propio Watanabe lo ve con cierta cautela. “Llevará mucho tiempo”, anunció. Esa unidad también quieren que tenga una relación con la pista. Y Alonso ya ha adelantado que ve buenas noticias salir desde la fábrica de Honda. “Están pasando muchas cosas entre bastidores en Japón y soy razonablemente optimista de cara al año que viene en lo que respecta al motor”, lanzó. Un mensaje positivo entre dudas con el motor actual, la revisión de Honda antes de Austin y un fin de campaña que será duro. Y, claro, viene justo después de una información de la BBC que casi señaló un ultimátum de Lawrence Stroll. Al magnate no le temblaría el pulso para cambiar de suministrador de unidad de potencia con Red Bull y Mercedes en la pole para poder hacerles un cliente en lugar de ser el oficial de Honda. Eso sólo lo dirá el futuro y 2027 dirá si hay algo de cierto.
